summary: On-demand tenant activity ledger delta for Subject Access Request with verifiable offsets and event-provenance
description: Customer request: MonetaBank compliance team opened a SAR and asked for a compact, ordered delta export of tenant activity for their tenant (tenant_id: moneta-prod-74) covering the requested date range. They require verifiable offsets (resume tokens), per-record provenance hashes, and a signed manifest that can be used in legal review. Request must preserve ordering across partitions and include mapping of internal fields to their SIEM column names.
impact: Customer cannot complete their GDPR subject access response until the archive bundle with provenance manifest is delivered. This is blocking MonetaBank's legal timeline; they have requested proof-of-delivery and a checksum to attest ordering.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer requested export via compliance portal and uploaded SAR reference number SAR-2026-031; 2) Support attempted to generate a compact delta using existing /exports/on-demand flow for tenant moneta-prod-74; 3) Generated package showed unordered event sequences when validated against customer's resume token expectations; 4) Support halted and escalated to engineering for manifest hash and ordering guarantees.

investigation_notes: Initial export produced files partitioned by shard-id; customer expects single chronologically-ordered delta across all shards for legal review.

Confirmed resume-token gaps: investigation traced to background compaction window that ran during the export job and merged events out of the immediate ordering. Compaction is intended but can alter visible offsets for delta-style exports.

Service artifact: archive-service v1.13.2 uses non-deterministic shard-level boundary ordering while compaction completes. Engineering recommended generating an ordered replay stream from the event-ledger instead of simple shard concatenation.
Auth check: S3 bundle was created with correct tenant-scoped KMS key and ACLs; signing key was not attached because the signing subtask failed to reach the hsm-service due to a transient 503 timeout.
Hypothesis: Two concurrent operations (compaction + on-demand export) caused visible offset gaps and prevented signing step from attaching ed25519 signature to manifest.
Workaround considered: pause compaction for the tenant window or generate replay stream from immutable event-ledger snapshot (recommended).

resolution_notes: Delivered ordered replay stream generated from immutable event-ledger snapshot for tenant moneta-prod-74. Manifest includes per-record provenance hashes (sha256), resume tokens, ed25519 signature (ed-key-7), KMS wrapping key fingerprint and chain-of-custody timestamps. Support provided mapping CSV to customer's SIEM columns and a short verification script. Customer confirmed receipt and validated ordering against SAR offsets.
root_cause: Compaction scheduler ran overlapping with on-demand export, leading to visible gaps in shard-concatenated delta. Additionally, a transient HSM 503 prevented automated manifest signing which delayed delivery until a manual retry.
next_steps: Short-term: Add export path that streams from immutable event-ledger snapshot to guarantee chronological ordering for SAR/legal exports.
Mid-term: Add pre-export compaction quiesce option for on-demand tenant exports to avoid overlap with maintenance windows.
Long-term: Add automated retry with circuit-breaker for signing subtask and alerting for HSM 5xx errors (INT ticket to follow).
Documentation: Update compliance playbook and support runbook with step-by-step verification checklist and sample verification scripts for customers.
